runners_data.name: Acclamation Star
runners_data.comment: Scored by three and a half lengths on debut at Bath over today's trip on firm ground, so conditions suit, and Oisin Murphy takes the ride with more improvement expected — but ranked 22nd of 25 on our figures, making this a lightly raced runner who needs to find a good deal more to figure here.

runners_data.name: Bated Benevolence
runners_data.comment: Debut winner at Nottingham — asserting late over 1½ lengths on good ground at 6f — but ranked 23rd of 25 on our figures, and stepping up markedly in class here means considerable further progress is required to trouble these.

runners_data.name: Blue Sign
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and yet to win, Blue Sign showed fair debut promise when finishing fourth at Lingfield, and has course-going experience to call on, but drawn 12 and ranked last on our figures, this 5f performer on good to firm looks firmly up against it.

runners_data.name: Crazy Cubana
runners_data.comment: Finished strongly to win a novice at Nottingham on debut 41 days ago, showing ability at today's trip on good ground — but improvement is very much required stepping up into this grade, and a ranking of 20th of 25 on our figures makes it hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Dark Issue
runners_data.comment: Decisive on debut, taking a Goodwood maiden by five-and-a-half lengths on good ground over today's trip 27 days ago, and the quality of the yard demands respect — though stepping straight from a single run into a field of 25 from stall 7 off 128 lb is the unknown.

runners_data.name: Dee's Funny Girl
runners_data.comment: Won on debut at Thirsk, pulling clear late over a trip she handles, but stepping up to this level asks more questions — and while 6f looks likely to bring further improvement, that potential is untested at this grade.

runners_data.name: Desert Sands
runners_data.comment: Beaten seven lengths on debut at Newbury 18 days ago, Desert Sands showed a degree of promise but looks out of her depth in this company — stall 24 in a large field, winless, and ranked 21 of 25 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Dubai Charm
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in two recent starts, Dubai Charm lines up from stall 21 carrying 128 lb, ranked 24th of 25 on our figures. The form — a six-length third last time — suggests meaningful improvement is needed here, though course-and-distance experience and proven going conditions offer slim consolation.

runners_data.name: Glamorize
runners_data.comment: Ran second on debut at Lingfield, beaten four-and-a-quarter lengths, so there's a foundation to build on — yet to win and a significant step forward is required stepping up to 6f, though the in-form yard and experience on today's going offer some encouragement from stall 22.

runners_data.name: Hidden Gift
runners_data.comment: Beaten just half a length on its only recent outing at Ripon, Hidden Gift clearly has ability despite being yet to win, and the step up to 6f looks a natural fit — drawing stall 19 carrying 128 lb, it could outrun its odds at a price.

runners_data.name: Jolivette
runners_data.comment: Promising on debut, winning narrowly at Newmarket on first start, and connections boast a strong record at this track; the step up in class and competition is the obvious question mark, but she handles today's trip and going, and her rating of 110 makes her one to respect.

runners_data.name: King's Prize
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced but promising, King's Prize won with plenty in reserve on debut and should appreciate this stiff 6f on good ground; the 54-day absence is a minor query from stall 13, though top connections expect further improvement.

runners_data.name: Kochella
runners_data.comment: Shaped with real promise on debut when just denied at Pontefract 17 days ago, fading only late to finish a close third — encouragingly fresh and handles today's trip. Yet to win, and stepping into a field of 25 from stall 2 makes this a stiff task despite likely improvement to come.

runners_data.name: Libertango
runners_data.comment: Impressive on debut at Leicester, winning a maiden with plenty to spare over today's trip and going, Libertango arrives here 24 days later in fine trim for top connections; the step up in grade is the key test from stall 3 in this 25-runner field.

runners_data.name: Light Of Dawn
runners_data.comment: Burst onto the scene at Carlisle 11 days ago, winning on debut with plenty held back under a gentle ride — the step to better ground here suits, and experience over the trip is a positive, though stall 23 in a field of 25 gives pause for thought.

runners_data.name: Love Is
runners_data.comment: Ran second last time on debut at Goodwood, then went one better to open her account, so the form trajectory is encouraging; acts on today's conditions over the trip, but stepping up in class means more will be needed here.

runners_data.name: Magnesium
runners_data.comment: Improved markedly after a debut seventh to land a Kempton novice over course-and-distance last time out, and the 30-day turnaround looks fine, but stepping up to this level from a 3/4-length novice win leaves Magnesium with plenty to prove from stall 16 carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Ron's Angel
runners_data.comment: Showed a determined attitude to land a Lingfield maiden last time by a short margin, and handles today's trip on this surface, but stepping up into Group 3 company is a significantly tougher ask for a horse whose debut level still needs proving at this grade.

runners_data.name: Roxelina
runners_data.comment: Plenty to like about Roxelana's debut third at Windsor — beaten just 2l — and with good connections expecting improvement, the step forward looks there for the taking; yet to win, stall 25 in a 25-runner field, and 128lb demand patience.

runners_data.name: Silent Beauty
runners_data.comment: Bolted up by four lengths on debut at Yarmouth, suggesting plenty more to come, and the step back to 6f on good-to-soft ground plays to her strengths; the key question is whether that single run leaves her vulnerable to more seasoned rivals.

runners_data.name: Sun Goddess
runners_data.comment: Sun Goddess arrives here in fine fettle — winning a Curragh maiden by five lengths last time despite early interference showed real class — and with Ballydoyle's juveniles in top form this week and a top course jockey aboard, she looks the one to beat over this stiff six furlongs.

runners_data.name: Tall Trees
runners_data.comment: Fifth on debut at Newbury — beaten four lengths when the race clicked late — Tall Trees is yet to win but showed enough greenness-masking ability to suggest improvement is likely; acts on today's ground and trip, and 18 days on should sharpen the mind.

runners_data.name: Topaz
runners_data.comment: Beaten a neck on debut at Newmarket, Topaz shapes as one with clear upside from stall 15, and today's trip at this distance suits — yet to win and remains unexposed, so the 128 lb burden is the main question mark against further improvement.

runners_data.name: Valentina Bella
runners_data.comment: Consecutive wins, the latest a Listed success at Vichy, mark Valentina Bella as a serious contender here, and stepping up to 6f from stall 1 in this 25-runner field should pose no issues; the main concern is whether the ground proves quicker than ideal.

runners_data.name: What A Girl Wants
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up and Listed-placed, What A Girl Wants clearly has ability, but remains yet to win and ranks 18th of 25 on our figures. Stall 14 carrying 128 lb, the smart filly faces a stiff task here despite proven effectiveness over today's trip.

races.name: Commonwealth Cup (Group 1) (No Geldings)

runners_data.name: Albert Einstein
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's colt won twice over 6f on good in his last two runs before a mixed campaign this year; a natural front-front prominent racer who the congestion in this field will push further back than he'd like, making his task materially harder than his OR-107 suggests.
runners_data.comment: Went agonisingly close when a neck away in Listed company at Newbury last time, and with a top course jockey aboard and more to offer, Albert Einstein shapes as a serious threat here; the worry is whether that consistent recent form can be converted into the win column.

runners_data.name: Aspect Island
runners_data.note: Has headgear (visor) fitted and ran only three days ago — freshness is a potential concern — and while he wants to race close to the pace, the crowded prominent zone means he is realistically looking at a midfield berth rather than his ideal position tracking the leader.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts, Aspect Island steps back up to 6f in a first-time visor, and there's a case it wasn't entirely seen to best effect when beaten five lengths in a Group 1 here last time — yet stepping up in class looks the chief obstacle despite proven versatility over the trip.

runners_data.name: Brussels
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie fitted and has placed twice on good-to-firm going over 5f, but his recent form (6th, 4th) since his spring campaign is patchy; a genuine pace-seeking type who will be squeezed out of his natural spot by the depth of this prominent division.
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces applied for the first time as Brussels, yet to win in his last five starts, returns 27 days on from a beaten fourth in the Sandy Lane Group 2 — a performance that mirrored his three-year-old debut. Handles today's trip and conditions, but whether he can rediscover the level he showed as a juvenile remains the question.

runners_data.name: Charles Darwin
runners_data.note: The most impressive of Aidan O'Brien's team with three wins from five starts at 5-6f on good, wears a hood, and is a natural front-seeker who is actually capable of securing a prime position just off Venetian Sun — the key question is whether he can reproduce his spring brilliance in a field of this quality.
runners_data.comment: Consistent winner of four of his last five starts, Charles Darwin arrives in fine fettle and is well-suited by today's trip and conditions — blinkers added for the first time could sharpen him up after a flat reappearance. The worry is whether that nine-length defeat still lingers.

runners_data.name: Coppull
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's progressive sort won over this exact course and distance on good 49 days ago and has an excellent record of 3W from 5 starts at 6f on good going; well-drawn or not, he is a genuine prominent type with strong claims in the dominant race shape.
runners_data.comment: Placed in the Middle Park and a neck winner of the Commonwealth Cup Trial on this course last time out, Coppull clearly handles today's conditions and trip well — though 49 days off the track and a mark of 110 leave questions about whether he returns to that peak.

runners_data.name: Division
runners_data.note: William Haggas and James Doyle combine with a horse who has a 2W record at 6f on good and races handily — the drop to third in his last two is concerning but this track and trip suits his rolling prominent style if the early fractions are honest.
runners_data.comment: Beaten three lengths when runner-up in a Group 2 last time, Division arrives fit and proven over course and distance from stall 3 in this field of 22, but a tall, powerfully built colt who likely needs further to fulfil his potential may find this trip just sharp enough.

runners_data.name: Havana Hurricane
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Eve Johnson Houghton who has three wins from eight starts on good but is bumped into midfield by the sheer volume of pace in this race; the style-fit discount is real and his OR-101 makes him vulnerable at this level.
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer that ran to form on return from a break with a third in the Carnarvon Stakes at Newbury 34 days ago, showing it handles the trip and conditions. Yet to win in its last five starts, though, and may need more to trouble the market leaders from stall 10.

runners_data.name: My Calyx Cen
runners_data.note: French raider trained by Patrik Olave Valdivielso with a 3W from 5 starts record including a win on Flat stable going; 66 days since last run is the key fitness question, and while a natural pace-racer, the overcrowded prominent zone leaves him exposed to being outmanoeuvred for position.
runners_data.comment: Consistent profile – four wins in last five starts including a narrow Group 3 success at Chantilly – but our figures rank this well down the field, and that French form will need a significant step forward to trouble today's rivals.

runners_data.name: Northern Champion
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's lightly-raced sort has won at 6f and 7f on good but finished 10th at this course last time and hasn't run for 83 days — the long break and the crowded prominent zone are both concerns for a horse who wants to race handily.
runners_data.comment: Beaten eight lengths in a Group 1 last time, Northern Champion heads into this ranked well down our assessments and faces a stiff ask stepping back out after 83 days; the two wins earlier in Dubai show there is ability here, but a bounce-back is needed against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Outfielder
runners_data.note: Wesley Ward's hold-up horse wears a tongue-tie and has limited European form (4th over 6f on good last time), coming off a 41-day break; genuine hold-up type who needs the pace to be truly honest over 6f at Ascot — the controlled tempo is his chief enemy here.
runners_data.comment: Tongue tie applied for the first time and 41 days between runs raise questions, and at 128lb from stall 21 this needs to defy our figures as a 19th-ranked runner — though genuine pace and back-to-back wins suggest it's not without ability at this trip on fast ground.

runners_data.name: Rock On Thunder
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's horse wears a hood (p), has a decent place record but no win at 6f on good, and his last six runs show a horse who finds the line elusive despite travelling well — needs a stronger-than-expected gallop to peg back the prominent types.
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces fitted for the first time as Rock On Thunder attempts to reverse two below-par sixth-place finishes, yet to build on a promising Gimcrack effort; handles today's trip and conditions, though 128 lb from stall 22 is no easy ask.

runners_data.name: Samangan
runners_data.note: French-trained by Graffard with three wins on soft at 6f; the switch to good to firm is a legitimate concern given all five runs show soft or heavy-adjacent ground, and he will need to prove his class translates to genuinely fast conditions.
runners_data.comment: Effective over six or seven furlongs on cut ground and boasting three wins in its last five starts, Samangan's fourth-place finish in a Chantilly Group 3 latest shows ability, but ranked 20th of 22 on our figures, it simply looks to need more to get involved here.

runners_data.name: Song Of The Clyde
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's filly won twice at 6f on good and is bred for this track; a genuine prominent type with strong course-and-distance form who should be able to secure a handy berth even in this crowded race and has solid claims if the race is run at a moderate tempo.
runners_data.comment: Landed a Listed prize at Newbury last time out and remains on the upgrade, though a large field from stall 2 adds a tactical question mark; acts on today's trip and going, and 128 lb looks the main test of whether progress continues.

runners_data.name: Super Soldier
runners_data.note: K R Burke's hold-up type ran only six days ago and his form reading 794-00 tells its own story — no wins at 6f on good in his recent run of form and the quick turnaround after a blank run makes him hard to support here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Super Soldier was well beaten at York just six days ago and that quick turnaround offers little encouragement. Carries 128 lb from stall 12, though he has form over today's trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Wise Approach
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby and William Buick's colt has an 8/8 record on good going over 6f, including wins at this track, and is the most consistent prominent horse in the race on a going basis — the 34-day break is standard and this profile is tailor-made for the dominant race shape.
runners_data.comment: Showed a return to form when four lengths off the pace in Listed company at Newbury last time, and acts on today's trip and going — but consecutive placed efforts since that sole recent win leave questions, and the 128lb burden from stall 15 asks plenty.

runners_data.name: Fitzella
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly has placed over 6f on good twice in five starts and is one of several naturally prominent types the field's density pushes towards midfield; James McDonald rides and is capable of finding a gap, but the style-fit adjustment is a real burden at this level.
runners_data.comment: Showed a flat effort when beaten four and a half lengths in a Listed fillies' contest at Goodwood last time, but was in solid nick before that and acts on this trip and ground; a capable pilot takes the ride from stall 16, though the class of this field makes things tough.

runners_data.name: Havana Anna
runners_data.note: Donnacha Aidan O'Brien's filly has won three from six at 5-6f on good and won last time out 33 days ago; a genuine pace-seeking type who, unlike many prominent rivals, has the profile and connections to actually secure her preferred position in this field.
runners_data.comment: Returning to form at just the right moment, Havana Anna took the Lacken Stakes (Group 3) at Naas by a head on her latest start 33 days ago — a tenacious effort that underlines her class at 5-6f on any ground. The unplaced run before that is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Kimi Rey
runners_data.note: Graffard's second string has won twice on heavy/soft-adjacent going and placed on good; the step up to Group 1 competition on fast turf at Ascot is a significant ask, and the redistribution from her natural prominent style makes her task harder still.
runners_data.comment: Placed in a Group 3 on her latest start, but that was on cut in the ground and conditions here pose a question; others hold a clear edge on our figures, leaving Kimi Rey tough to fancy despite consistent recent form.

runners_data.name: Midnight Tango
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly is a genuine hold-up type with a 2nd in her most recent run and the form to suggest she stays well at 6f on good; 49-day break is fine, and she is one of the more credible closers in a race with a controlled early pace — the tempo being slow enough to let prominents get home is her chief threat.
runners_data.comment: Caught close up when beaten a neck in a Group 3 Commonwealth Cup Trial here over today's trip on suitable ground latest, Midnight Tango returns after 49 days yet to score in five recent starts, and carrying 125lb from stall 17, there's more needed to challenge at this level.

runners_data.name: Spicy Marg
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's filly won at 6f on good three runs ago and is a natural pace-racer, but the 8th and 3rd on her last two runs suggest she has lost her spring form, and the crowded prominent zone leaves little room for error in a 22-runner Group 1.
runners_data.comment: Shaped well when a 4½-length third in the Sandy Lane Stakes last time, and Spicy Marg's record over this trip and going underlines a genuine versatility that keeps her competitive; held-up tactics and a tendency to run her race consistently make her a solid each-way player, though ranking 11 of 22 suggests improvement is needed.

runners_data.name: Venetian Sun
runners_data.note: K R Burke's OR-115 top-rated horse is the sole confirmed front-runner and the pace map's axis; four wins from seven starts including two at 6f on good means she has the class and the experience to dictate on this surface, and her ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the single most important tactical factor in this race.
runners_data.comment: Venetian Sun bolted up in a Group 2 last time by three lengths and boasts the class and versatility to go on any ground over today's trip — a 27-day turnaround looks straightforward, and from stall 13 this looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Zanthos
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's colt won twice at 7f on good before a 9th last time out; Oisin Murphy takes the ride and the step back to 6f is interesting — he is a natural prominent type with the class to be competitive if he recaptures his spring form, though the last run gives pause.
runners_data.comment: Shaped like a smart filly on her best form — two wins in her last four starts including a runner-up effort — but that ninth last time, beaten nine lengths in a Group 1 at Longchamp on deep ground over a mile, clouds the picture; back to six furlongs from stall 1 in a field of 22 today.

races.paceDynamic: Venetian Sun is the one confirmed front-runner in a 22-runner Group 1 field and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival prepared to go stride-for-stride from the off — this creates a genuinely sustainable, measured gallop rather than a contested burn-up. Behind her, a cluster of natural prominent types including Charles Darwin, Coppull, Division, Wise Approach, Havana Anna, Song Of The Clyde, Samangan and Zanthos will press for the early positions, generating a solid but not frantic pace through the first three furlongs. Hold-up horses Outfielder, Rock On Thunder and Midnight Tango will be asked to come from off the pace on a track where Good to Firm ground at Ascot over six furlongs historically rewards those who travel prominently and quicken in the final two furlongs. The tactical verdict is clear: horses that can settle just off the controlled lead — genuine prominent-to-midfield types with a strong cruising speed and a turn of foot — are best placed, with those forced deepest carrying the steepest burden against this surface and trip profile. The field holds substantially more front-running and prominent types than the race can physically accommodate; among those redistributed to midfield on the map, Charles Darwin, Coppull and Wise Approach are best equipped by class and form to actually secure their natural berth close to the pace.

watchPoints.text: Venetian Sun must be tracked from the stalls — if she is slow away or another horse challenges her for the lead in the first furlong, the pace dynamic changes entirely and the control scenario collapses.

With 22 runners on a straight 6f track, monitor the draw heavily at race time — horses drawn high may be forced wide in the early scramble for position, materially hurting the several prominent types who need a clean break to secure their berth.

Samangan's record is entirely on soft-to-heavy ground; if the going is riding faster than the posted Good to Firm suggests from the Ascot report, his chance may be significantly overstated at the prices.

Outfielder's chance hinges almost entirely on the early pace being genuinely strong rather than controlled — if Venetian Sun dictates without pressure, Wesley Ward's hold-up horse has minimal realistic chance of closing the gap on fast ground.

races.name: Duke Of Edinburgh Stakes (Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Burdett Road
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with strong form over 2m and 1m6f; drops back to 1m4f here which could be sharp, though he ran 2nd over 1m6f at Ascot on Good recently — jockey Luke Morris and trainer James Owen combination at 9/55 over 14 days is unremarkable; 83 days off so freshness could be an asset or a risk.|
runners_data.comment: Shaped with some promise at shorter trips and acts on the ground, but Burdett Road is winless in recent starts and returning after 83 days off; dropping back from two miles into a handicap off a mark of 105 suits, though eight rivals hold a superior ranking.

runners_data.name: Ambiente Friendly
runners_data.note: Long absence of 307 days (19 since jockey claim) is a major question mark for James Owen; hold-up style suits a strongly-run race and he has form at 1m6f on similar ground, but the layoff and the tongue-tie (hg:p) make confidence hard to justify.|
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces fitted for the first time as connections search for improvement, and Ambiente Friendly has shown ability at this trip on a sound surface — but a winless recent run of five starts and a mark that looks stern make progress hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Mondo Man
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner returning after a massive 407-day break; Gary & Josh Moore have won with fresh horses and Christophe Soumillon is a top booking, but the distance form at 1m6f on soft is questionable over this shorter trip on quicker ground — needs to bounce back first time out after over a year off.|
runners_data.comment: Once a high-class Flat performer and interesting on a return to familiar conditions over today's trip, Mondo Man arrives on a short break in decent prior form with a notable jockey booking catching the eye — though jumping errors and a tendency to do too much early remain the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Warrant Holder
runners_data.note: William Buick's mount is the race's sole confirmed front-runner and has won twice recently including over 1m2f at Goodwood; stepping up markedly in trip to 1m4f is a genuine stamina question, and the [STYLE_FIT=0.90] flag reflects that he is operating here in a field that will want to push him back — if his jumping ability holds, he sets the race up on his terms.|
runners_data.comment: Warrant Holder arrives here in fine fettle — a winner at York on latest outing, scoring comfortably in a handicap off a 5lb lower mark, and the trainer is firing — though first-time headgear and a 6lb rise in the weights will test whether that York effort can be matched at this level.

runners_data.name: Emit
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for Joseph Patrick O'Brien, who is in strong form at 8/60 over 14 days; prominent style suits this shape and he has placed form at 1m4f on Good, though he hasn't won in a run string of 2-4-3-5-4 suggesting consistency without finishing.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts but shaped with promise on its latest outing at today's trip, and first-time headgear plus a top course jockey could sharpen the response; the 137 lb burden is the main concern at a mark of 104.

runners_data.name: Plage De Havre
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partner for Andrew Balding (12/65 over 14 days — strong yard in form); won over 1m2f on Good recently and prominent style is ideal for this Warrant Holder-led scenario — the concern is whether 1m4f fully stretches his stamina at Ascot.|
runners_data.comment: Kept on to finish a sound 3rd last time out over a course-and-distance he handles well, and a top trainer holds an edge here; yet the 135 lb burden and a mark of 102 leave little room for error, and that pulled-up run lurks in recent memory.

runners_data.name: Nightime Dancer
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon runner prominent in style with solid Ascot 1m4f Good form (4th last time); Sean Levey knows the yard well, and the consistent placed form (2nd, 3rd, 4th) suggests a horse that performs without winning — likely to be competitive without necessarily sealing it.|
runners_data.comment: Placed in three of its last five starts and effective at today's trip on this surface, Nightime Dancer showed enough on handicap debut at Newmarket last time — beaten five lengths into fourth — to suggest a forward move is feasible, and there's a class edge behind that 113 rating; yet to win in recent starts remains the concern.

runners_data.name: French Duke
runners_data.note: Hamad Al Jehani yard at only 2/15 over 14 days is weak; Jamie Spencer is a master at riding waiting races but French Duke's style is prominent — Spencer may adapt his tactics but the yard's current form gives pause; 132-day break is notable.|
runners_data.comment: Absent 132 days and ranked well towards the foot of the field on our figures, French Duke faces a stiff task off 135 lb — though the sixth here a year ago came on reappearance, and he handles today's trip and conditions well enough to be considered a place outsider at best.

runners_data.name: Omni Man
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle rides for the in-form Joseph Patrick O'Brien stable (8/62 over 14 days); won over 1m2f on Good at Cork which is the best recent form, but prominent style suits a field this size only if he gets a handy berth — headgear (hg:t) suggests he needs to be kept focused.|
runners_data.comment: Tuned up after 40 days off and fitted with a first-time hood, Omni Man has shown versatility across a range of trips and conditions — and ran with credit at this meeting last year — but the two most recent efforts have been disappointing, and a mark of 101 makes life tough in this grade.

runners_data.name: Hopewell Rock
runners_data.note: James Doyle for George Boughey (3/31 over 14 days — modest strike rate); consistent placer at 1m2f on Good and Soft, and the step up to 1m4f is the key unknown — prominent style ideally placed for this shape if the trip doesn't stretch him.|
runners_data.comment: Held every chance if building on a comeback third at Newmarket, where it was beaten just two lengths off this mark; Hopewell Rock handles today's trip and conditions well, and our top rating of 118 underlines its claims, though it remains winless in its last five starts.

runners_data.name: Opportunity
runners_data.note: James McDonald takes a strong booking for William Haggas (11/46 — the best-strike-rate yard represented here); naturally a prominent racer who has been redistributed to midfield because so many horses want that position — McDonald's tactical intelligence gives him a better chance than most of pushing forward from an awkward spot.|
runners_data.comment: Opportunity bolted up at Carlisle 20 days ago, winning a handicap by two and a quarter lengths off a mark 8lb lower than today's, and this big colt handles the trip and going well — stepping back into Group company after that handicap win is the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Military Academy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Jane Chapple-Hyam (1/14 over 14 days — quiet yard); headgear (hg:b) suggests a horse that needs settling, and the recent form string of 2-3-0-5-5-7 reads as a horse in steady decline — 13 days since last run is quick turnaround.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last six starts and ranked 16 of 19 on our figures, Military Academy arrives in first-time blinkers after trailing the field at Epsom 13 days ago; inconsistency and a tough mark make this hard to fancy, even if today's trip and conditions are familiar.

runners_data.name: Tuscan Hills
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar yard at 1/10 over 14 days and David Egan rides; hold-up style and a recent 0 in form is hard to get past — the 96-day break and inconsistent trip range (8f to 1m4f) make him a lottery, though he did win over 1m on Soft.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last four starts and ranked 17th of 19 on our figures, Tuscan Hills returns after 96 days off the track with stamina still to prove — the deep ground finding it out last time at the Curragh doesn't inspire confidence at these weights.

runners_data.name: Insanity
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan for Alan King (3/11 over 14 days); habitual front-rank performer whose form shows 11 prominent positions in last 15 runs — placed here in midfield by redistribution, the [STYLE_FIT=0.93] flag is significant, and King will need Ryan to push forward early to recapture a comfortable position; consistent recent placed form on Good is encouraging if he gets his spot.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent placer yet to win in its last five starts, Insanity shaped well on return at Pontefract last time, going down by just over two lengths off this exact mark; back up to 12f looks a positive angle, though the 59-day absence and 132lb are the key questions.

runners_data.name: Dain Ma Nut In
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for Lucinda Russell & Michael Scudamore (1/17 over 14 days); this horse has won six of his last 15 races from the front and is a thorough front-runner pushed into midfield by the redistribution — 120 days off adds another layer of difficulty, and on a circuit as competitive as Ascot, reclaiming a forward position from a filed draw will be tough for Keane.|
runners_data.comment: Seventh on latest start over 11f and absent for 120 days, Dain Ma Nut In needs to bounce back sharply — stamina at today's trip also remains unproven — though a notable jockey booking lends some interest, and this front-runner has shown effectiveness over shorter on a sound surface.

runners_data.name: Nesthorn
runners_data.note: Neil Callan for George Baker (1/7 over 14 days); three consecutive 7th-place finishes in last three starts after two wins suggest a horse that has gone off the boil — hold-up style and form at 1m2f on Good raises trip doubts at 1m4f.|
runners_data.comment: Three straight seventh-place finishes leave Nesthorn hard to fancy, and our figures rank it last of 19 in this field — a significant gap to the official mark of 99. The return from a 78-day absence adds uncertainty, though there are two recent wins on the record and the trip suits.

runners_data.name: Teumessias Fox
runners_data.note: Jason Watson rides for Andrew Balding (12/63); veteran seven-year-old whose last five runs have all come over 1m2f on Standard going (all-weather) — the switch to 1m4f on turf Good to Firm is a significant profile change, and the form (5-3-5-3-7) doesn't inspire confidence on turf.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Teumessias Fox at least shaped with credit last time — beaten three and a half lengths off a mark just 1lb higher than today's — and handles this trip and going, but held-up tactics leave him vulnerable to stronger rivals here.

runners_data.name: Regal Ulixes
runners_data.note: P J McDonald for Andrew Balding, giving the yard a second string alongside Teumessias Fox; naturally a prominent racer redistributed to midfield given the crowded front end — headgear (hg:h) suggests a horse that can be keen, and form of 7-4-6-1-6 over 1m on Standard shows he acts on a flat track but the 1m4f trip on turf is a stretch.|
runners_data.comment: Keen tendencies cost Regal Ulixes at York 35 days ago, beaten four lengths off a 1lb higher mark, but the drop back to 12f looks a significant positive, and a top course trainer plus first-time headgear suggest connections are priming a bold showing.

runners_data.name: Serengeti
runners_data.note: Kieran Shoemark for Mike Murphy (2/11 over 14 days); won over 1m on Good 25 days ago which is the headline, but his redistribution from true hold-up to midfield reflects the crowded back end — career form includes a 28th-place finish and he was running over sprint trips not long ago; the [STYLE_FIT=0.92] flag is appropriate given his unusual profile for this trip and competition.|
runners_data.comment: Serengeti won a Windsor handicap last time by a head off a 1lb lower mark, first try at 10f in a tongue-tie, but stepping up to 12f leaves stamina unproven for a horse effective between 7-10f — ranked 15 of 19 on our figures, it's hard to get enthused.

races.paceDynamic: Warrant Holder is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, with William Buick in the saddle, is likely to stride into a clear lead and control a measured, sustainable gallop over Ascot's 1m4f on Good to Firm ground. Behind him, Emit, Plage De Havre, Nightime Dancer, French Duke, Omni Man, and Hopewell Rock all want to race prominently, creating a congested group chasing the leader rather than any genuine pressure on Warrant Holder's fractions. The result is a race likely to be run at a smooth, even tempo with no horse seriously burning Warrant Holder off the front — conditions that classically compress the field into a pack heading into the straight, making the race a stamina-and-finishing-kick contest rather than a true test of early pace. This shape favours prominent racers who can travel close to the pace without expending energy, and especially those with the ability to quicken from handy positions in the straight; genuine hold-up horses will struggle unless the tempo quickens enough to string the field out. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Opportunity, Insanity, Dain Ma Nut In, and Regal Ulixes are all natural front-rank horses who will be shuffled back into midfield, meaning those positions will be occupied by horses racing out of their comfort zone.

scenarios.body: If the pace genuinely hotens up in the middle stages and the field strings out, giving true hold-up horses a clear run through beaten horses late.

watchPoints.text: Warrant Holder's true stamina at 1m4f is completely untested — if he ties up in the final two furlongs after dictating from the front, watch for Plage De Havre and Emit to pounce as they track him throughout.|

The cluster of displaced prominent types — Opportunity, Insanity, Dain Ma Nut In — will all be pushing forward from the gates; watch the first two furlongs for a scrimmage that could unsettle runners immediately behind them and compromise the race for hold-up horses like Burdett Road.|

races.name: Coronation Stakes (Group 1) (Fillies)

runners_data.name: Balantina
runners_data.note: A progressive filly stepping up from six furlongs to a mile — her winning run over course-and-distance-relevant trips and five-from-six record on similar going make her a natural fit for this track and surface; Oisin Murphy adds further confidence from a prominent pitch after 231 days off, so fitness is the one question mark.
runners_data.comment: Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf Grade 1 winner last time out, she handled the step up to a mile with authority on good ground — course and distance form checks out — but 231 days off the track and the demands of this stiff mile are the chief concerns.

runners_data.name: Black Caviar Gold
runners_data.note: Visor-wearing filly who naturally races up with the pace but is displaced into midfield here because too many prominent types are fighting for the same ground — her best form came on softer surfaces and her recent Guineas fourth on good leaves a going query on this fast ground.
runners_data.comment: Tried Group 1 company last time and kept on to finish fourth, beaten six lengths at the Curragh — honest enough, but our figures rank this filly bottom of the field and consistent form simply doesn't stretch to winning at this level; the first-time visor at least offers a wildcard.

runners_data.name: Moon Target
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's filly has been off 252 days and, though she won first time out this season, her most recent effort was a distant eighth on good ground — a natural front-runner squeezed out of her favoured position by race shape, she faces both a fitness unknown and a tactical disadvantage from having to race in an unnatural berth.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way out in a Group 1 on her latest start, Moon Target faces a stiff winning task after a 252-day absence, though she acts on today's conditions, has scope over longer trips as a three-year-old, and a place claim remains live.

runners_data.name: Precise
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore on the Aidan O'Brien filly who holds five wins from seven runs on good ground and an outstanding 5/6 prominent-style record — she is the standout prominent type to track True Love's uncontested lead and her Guineas form reads better than most in this line-up.
runners_data.comment: Decisive winner of the Irish 1,000 Guineas at the Curragh last time out, pulling clear by 2½ lengths with a sharp burst of speed that marked her out as the class act here; bypassing the Oaks to take her chance underlines connections' confidence, and she acts on today's conditions.

runners_data.name: Rose Ghaiyyath
runners_data.note: A Richard Hughes three-year-old who has only one win from four starts on ground faster than soft, making the Good to Firm conditions a genuine concern — pushed into midfield by race shape despite her naturally forward-going tendencies, the combination of compromised position and suspect going profile dampens her claims significantly.
runners_data.comment: Beaten eight lengths in Listed company at Goodwood last time, and with a ranking of eighth of nine in the field, Rose Ghaiyyath looks hard to fancy here; the top jockey's return is a plus, but there are real doubts about whether she's good enough or sharp enough to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Sukanya
runners_data.note: The race's sole genuine hold-up performer, Jack Channon's filly won over seven furlongs on good ground last time and ran a clear second at the same trip — she needs the pace to be true and sustained to deliver her finishing effort from off the bridle, and a controlled True Love-led race may not generate enough early tempo to bring her into play.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time in a Group 1 on her most recent start, Sukanya has a bit to prove at this level and ranks seventh of nine on our figures; the earlier win and proven course-and-distance record offer some encouragement, but she remains hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Timeforshowcasing
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane's mount is a natural front-runner who has won twice at a mile but is shoe-horned into a midfield role by the dynamics of this field — she produced a 16th last time on good ground over course which is hard to ignore, though her soft-ground mile wins show she can stay the trip when conditions soften.
runners_data.comment: Boasts course-and-distance form and clearly handles today's going, with three wins in its last five starts including a Group 2 success on soft ground last time out — but stepping back up to Group 1 company represents a stiffer ask, and our rating of 110 leaves her with ground to make up on the market leaders from stall 9.

runners_data.name: Touleen
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows' filly is consistent and comes here on the back of a second at Goodwood — her two-from-two record on good going and solid prominent-style performance profile make her a genuine contender to sit just off the pace and respond when the race quickens; Saffie Osborne takes the ride.
runners_data.comment: Beaten just 4½ lengths in a Group 1 Guineas last time, Touleen brings strong Group-race form to this contest — trainer in good nick and the trip and going both suit — though that recent sixth on the back of a 47-day break is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: True Love
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's confirmed front-runner is set to lead from flag to finish on a pace-friendly straight mile, and her 5/9 win rate on similar going underscores her effectiveness in these conditions — the style-fit tag acknowledges she may be somewhat one-dimensional at the head of affairs in a Group 1, but the uncontested lead is a significant tactical advantage.
runners_data.comment: Proven over today's trip and ground, True Love arrives on the back of three wins in her last five starts and a close second in Group 1 company at the Curragh, showing she remains firmly at this level; the one query is whether she can overturn the form with the market rival she was behind there.

races.paceDynamic: True Love is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival willing to challenge her from the gate, she is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over Ascot's straight mile. Precise and Balantina are the natural prominent types best placed to track her through the early and middle stages, sitting close enough to pounce without burning fuel chasing a contested lead. The field holds more prominent-minded runners than can all secure that position — Timeforshowcasing, Moon Target, Black Caviar Gold and Rose Ghaiyyath are all natural front-to-prominent types but will be shuffled back into a midfield role against their instinct, with Timeforshowcasing and Black Caviar Gold most likely to press hardest for whatever berths remain behind True Love. A steady-to-fair pace set by a single, unchallenged leader on a sound surface historically rewards horses travelling prominently with a turn of foot in the final two furlongs — the shape firmly favours a close-tracking prominent racer who can quicken off the pace rather than a genuine hold-up performer.

scenarios.body: If True Love leads without serious pressure and the pace remains honest but controlled, allowing a close-tracking rival to strike smoothly.

scenarios.body: If True Love slows the race into a near-sprint, compressing the field and allowing midfield runners to close the gap before a final-furlong dash.

watchPoints.text: True Love's early stride pattern from the stalls — if she jumps cleanly and immediately opens up uncontested, the controlled-pace prominent scenario crystallises rapidly and Precise and Balantina become the ones to beat.

Watch the crowded early position battle between Timeforshowcasing, Black Caviar Gold, Moon Target and Rose Ghaiyyath — any bumping or checking as they compete for limited forward berths could cost them lengths they cannot recover on a flat, straight track.

Balantina returns after 231 days off; if she travels lazily or needs time to find her stride in the early furlongs, her prominent pitch could be wasted before the race reaches its critical phase past halfway.

Sukanya is the only true hold-up horse in the field — monitor whether True Love's early tempo is genuinely strong enough to create the pace scenario required for a late run, as a sedate gallop will leave Sukanya with nowhere to aim before the furlong pole.

Rose Ghaiyyath has only one win from four starts on going quicker than soft — check the going sticks at the time of race; if the ground dries further toward firm, her chances diminish materially regardless of race shape.

races.name: Sandringham Stakes (Handicap) (Fillies)

runners_data.name: Awaken
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, yet rated OR=101 and dropping to 8f from a recent run over 7f, she can likely set a controlled, unhurried gallop — 65 days off is a slight fitness query with Billy Loughnane aboard for Boughey, but her tactical position is unrivalled in this field.
runners_data.comment: Proven over this trip and ground, Awaken showed ability when second and winning in recent starts, but that Group 3 flop last time out raises questions, and a mark of 101 won't make handicap life straightforward after 65 days off.

runners_data.name: Mubasimah
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's filly returns 19 days after a disappointing Sandown run, but 2W2P in similar going with James Doyle aboard suggests she remains capable; a natural prominent type who will need to find her position quickly in a bunched field.
runners_data.comment: Mubasimah arrives on the back of a close-up Group 2 effort at Chantilly that arguably overstates her current level, but she acts on this surface over this trip, a top trainer handles the course well, and her handicap debut opens new doors — the weight of 134lb is the main question.

runners_data.name: Hope Queen
runners_data.note: K R Burke has fired this filly in twice this season winning both starts over 7-8f on good ground, and Clifford Lee partners a horse who has been relentlessly progressive; 9f last time may have stretched her but the return to 8f looks ideal.
runners_data.comment: Ran well below her best on seasonal debut in a Group 1 last time, but that stiff task up to a mile looks best forgiven — back in handicap company over an effective seven furlongs on ground that suits, Hope Queen's back-to-back wins beforehand keep her firmly in this.

runners_data.name: Just Call Me Angel
runners_data.note: Three wins from 8f-plus runs and Ed Dunlop's record with fillies at this level inspires confidence; last run was a disappointing 7th over 10f and the step back to a flat Ascot mile looks a form retrieval play on Robert Havlin's book.
runners_data.comment: Winning form at this trip and going gives Just Call Me Angel some relevance, but a heavy defeat last time out — possibly failing to see out 10f in Listed company — and a ranking of 26th in a field of 30 makes her very hard to fancy at the weights despite that earlier Classic success.

runners_data.name: Spinning Lizzie
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan takes the ride on a filly who won over 8f at Sandown last time; her 10f run prior was respectable in good company and she is a prominent type who will want the gallop to be honest rather than falsely slow.
runners_data.comment: Spinning Lizzie showed her class when finishing a staying-on third in a Listed heat at Newmarket 47 days ago, and handles today's trip and conditions well, but that effort still leaves something to find here and a trainer firing at just 5% makes the timing tricky.

runners_data.name: Zooming
runners_data.note: William Haggas and Tom Marquand combine on an OR=96 filly who has not won beyond 7f and steps up in trip here — the 48-day break and lack of a clear 8f win tempers enthusiasm despite the yard's strong Royal Ascot record.
runners_data.comment: Zooming showed smart form across her last four starts, including a win and a runner-up, but disappointed badly at Listed level last time out; a return to a familiar trip and a bounce-back are both needed here, though her ability in good-to-soft conditions at least offers some encouragement from stall 9.

runners_data.name: Seet
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore on the John & Thady Gosden filly who has won her last two starts at 8f on good and standard ground; only three runs to her name but the upward trajectory and Moore booking make her one of the most interesting profiles in the race.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins, including a penalty success at Doncaster with plenty to spare 14 days ago, mark Seet as the one to beat here; effective at today's trip and going, with a top-class jockey aboard and a trainer firing at 29%, the 130lb burden looks the only question.

runners_data.name: Al Rateel
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with an unknown running style and a French trainer not firing heavily in the UK (0/5 T14); Warren Fentiman claims 3lbs which helps at OR=95, but the limited profile means this is a significant question mark in a deep field.
runners_data.comment: Narrowly beaten in a Group 3 at San Siro latest, but ranked bottom of this field on our figures and burdened with 129 lb from stall 24, Al Rateel faces a stiff ask stepping up in class again, despite proven effectiveness over a mile.

runners_data.name: Repel
runners_data.note: F-H Graffard sends over a filly who landed 6f on good and was second over 6f — the step up to 8f at Ascot is a genuine trip question for Colin Keane to solve, and she will need to settle better than her sprint-bred profile implies.
runners_data.comment: Decent recent form — two wins from its last four starts including a comfortable success last time, with that yard in sharp nick at 26% — though ranked 20th in a 30-runner field and drawn in stall 1, there's enough in its profile to take seriously at this trip and going.

runners_data.name: Mixed Feelings
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle partners a Joseph O'Brien filly whose sole win came over 8f on soft; her good-ground credentials are thinner and a 10f run last time suggests stamina won't be the concern, but the going may be her limiting factor.
runners_data.comment: Struggled to see out ten furlongs when fifth at Naas last time, and with our figures ranking her 25th of 30, she faces a stiff ask here; however, a return to a shorter trip could suit, and that prior win shows she retains ability on her day.

runners_data.name: Quiet Mutiny
runners_data.note: A Gavin Cromwell-trained filly who won over 6f on good, placed over 6f on soft — Gary Carroll rides but she has not yet proven herself over a flat mile and the notable step up in trip and grade is a query.
runners_data.comment: Beaten three-quarters of a length off a 1lb lower mark on its most recent outing, Quiet Mutiny has shown ability at this trip and still looks unexposed, but ranked 28th of 30 on our figures, this is a tough ask from stall 25 carrying 125lb.

runners_data.name: Glyfada
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's filly has won back-to-back over 8f and 10f on good ground, suggesting she stays well and finishes powerfully; Oisin Murphy is a significant booking and she may be sharper than her rating implies after a 38-day break.
runners_data.comment: Glyfada arrives here in fine nick after back-to-back wins, most recently at Killarney over today's trip, and handles this ground well across a range of distances. A notable jockey booking adds appeal, though she carries 125 lb from stall 31 and steps up sharply in class.

runners_data.name: True Test
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride but True Test has managed only a run of 2-0-4-2-13 in her last five, suggesting inconsistency; William Knight sends her fresh after 47 days but an OR=90 and modest recent form limit expectations in this field.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in recent starts, True Test arrives 47 days after finishing nine lengths back in a Group 1 at Newmarket — clearly outclassed there but running to form. Draws stall 13 carrying 124 lb, and while the distance and conditions suit, a stronger level of opposition is needed.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Breeze
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who landed 8f on good ground last time for Jane Chapple-Hyam — David Egan rides and she is one of very few authentic closers in this race, meaning she could be well positioned if the pace collapses in the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Harlequin Breeze showed a transformed display when bolting up by 4½ lengths at Leicester last time out and clearly thrives at this trip on a sound surface, making it a leading contender on a career-best effort; the step up into handicap company is the key question.

runners_data.name: Brigid's Well
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly carries cheekpieces and won over 8f on good ground — she is a natural prominent racer who the pace map has shifted rearward due to overcrowding near the front, and Jamie Spencer's ability to find pockets may offset that positioning challenge.
runners_data.comment: Tongue-tie applied for the first time and a drop to a mile in this handicap look the key positives for Brigid's Well, who shaped with promise at Listed level last time over a longer trip; her inconsistent recent efforts, however, suggest she'll need to find more.

runners_data.name: Blingy's Sister
runners_data.note: Another Hugo Palmer entry, also OR=88 after an OR=88 decline from a 6f win — Toby Moore claims 7lbs and she is a front-running type whose speed over 6-7f hasn't been tested over this extra ground; the pace map moves her back and the step up in trip adds further risk.
runners_data.comment: Beaten seven lengths at Group 3 level last time out when out of her depth, Blingy's Sister faces a stiff ask to bounce back from that run after 62 days off; she does stay this trip and handles the going, but her ceiling looks exposed.

runners_data.name: Tavana
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon rides this Edward Smyth-Osbourne filly who won over 7f on soft and has a mixed profile at OR=87; she is a genuine pace-wanting type pushed into the map's midfield due to overcrowding, and the trainer's low UK strike rate (0/6 T14) is unhelpful.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with some promise when fourth on a previous start but contributed little when beaten five lengths at Newbury 34 days ago, and with a career-high 121 lb from stall 26, this versatile sort — effective on multiple surfaces and at today's trip — faces a stiff task here.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Angel
runners_data.note: The second Chapple-Hyam runner, this time with Alexandra Egan claiming 7lbs — two wins from 7f on good ground and a bold-racing style that the field has squeezed back; she ran 22nd last time at Goodwood suggesting form is volatile.
runners_data.comment: Beaten favourite last time out before bouncing back to win a handicap by 2¼ lengths at Yarmouth off a 6lb lower mark, Harlequin Angel arrives 50 days later carrying 121lb from stall 22, and at a rating of 87 faces a stiffer task on our figures, ranked 23 of 30.

runners_data.name: Bintaziza
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's filly won twice over 8f on standard going but lacks a confirmed good-to-firm win in three starts; Ray Dawson rides and at OR=87 the rating is workable, but her pace-hungry style is mapped to the midfield and the going profile remains slightly uncertain.
runners_data.comment: Showed good closing speed when beaten two lengths on her handicap turf debut at Thirsk 19 days ago, and a top trainer in fine form gives her every chance to build on back-to-back wins; the worry is whether she can reproduce that from stall 32.

runners_data.name: Green Carrera
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien sends over a filly who won on good over 8f most recently with Mickael Barzalona taking the ride — two wins from 8f starts and a hold on good ground gives her solid credentials; a natural prominent type mapped back due to field size, Barzalona's positional nous gives her the best chance of recovering near the pace.
runners_data.comment: Compact and willing, Green Carrera arrives on the back of a narrow Curragh handicap win 26 days ago off a 5lb lower mark — now up in weight, drawn 30, and wearing a hood for the first time, our figures make this a tough ask at the foot of the rankings.

runners_data.name: She Commands
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly has won three from five including a 10f win on standard going — Jack Dace claims 5lbs and she is a prominent type whose redistribution to the hold-up position on the map is against her natural inclination, though the extra class may compensate.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins — including defying a penalty last time — mark She Commands as a progressive type with more in the locker as she settles into handicap company for a leading stable, though the 39-day break and a speed rating of 81 leave slight questions.

runners_data.name: Darn Hot Gallop
runners_data.note: James Tate's filly won twice over 7f on standard going and was 17th last time over 8f on good — Aurelien Lemaitre takes the ride but that last run is a concern, and as a prominent type mapped to midfield she faces a positional battle from the outset.
runners_data.comment: Beaten well out of contention on latest start at Newmarket, Darn Hot Gallop needs a sharp revival here, and our figures rank it well down a deep field of 30. Three wins in its last four starts show there's ability, and it handles today's trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Symbol Of Majesty
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden enter a second runner at OR=86 with Saffie Osborne aboard — won over 8f on good and standard, but she is a prominent racer mapped to the rear because of the overcrowded pace, and that positional compromise is her key hurdle.
runners_data.comment: Beaten just over two lengths on its latest start when conditions didn't quite suit, Symbol Of Majesty arrives here with two wins in its last three outings, handles today's trip and going, and has a trainer in fine fettle — though from stall 21 carrying 120 lb, it must overcome a moderate recent run.

runners_data.name: Lyrics Of Life
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa rides one of only two genuine hold-up horses in the field — Brian Meehan's filly has placed four times over 8f on good ground without winning, suggesting she finds a way to be in it late but may lack a winning punch.
runners_data.comment: Consistent enough in recent starts but yet to win in its last five, Lyrics Of Life pulled hard and emptied out late when third here most recently — 49 days on, the lack of progression is a concern for a midfield hope carrying 119 lb from stall 29.

runners_data.name: Passing Thought
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly won over 6f on soft and standard last time — Luke Morris partners but the form over faster ground and this more exacting distance profile is unproven; a pace-wanting type mapped to midfield adds a positional dimension.
runners_data.comment: Passing Thought won a handicap on comeback from a break at Wetherby last time off a 5lb lower mark than today's, so the rise in class is the query, but versatility on ground and a step up to this mile trip could unlock further improvement.

runners_data.name: Rosa Inglesa
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes and Harry Davies combine on an OR=85 filly whose one 8f win came on soft — the step to good-to-firm Ascot is a query, and as a prominent type compressed into the midfield she may struggle to get the position she needs.
runners_data.comment: Rosa Inglesa landed a Nottingham handicap by three lengths off a 9lb lower mark over this trip last time out, suggesting there's more to come from this tall filly — though she must now prove herself off a higher mark, and the step up in class from stall 19 makes this a stern examination.

runners_data.name: Spinning Around
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's second entry carries a hood and won over 7f on good — Wayne Lordan rides and she has been progressive in soft-ground form, but the three-from-seven record on good ground and the pace redistribution away from her natural front
runners_data.comment: Tongue-tied for the first time today and a winner at a lower mark last time out, Spinning Around has some form credentials, but at 94 on our figures — ranked near the foot of the field — and returning after 46 days, this is a hard one to get behind at any fancy price.

runners_data.name: Crownright
runners_data.comment: Crownright has placed in all three recent starts and, as a Frankel filly who should relish a large, competitive field, looks capable of stepping up on that placed form — our rating of 108 underlines the scope here. The key is whether she settles, having pulled hard at Leicester last time when second.

runners_data.name: Thankfully
runners_data.comment: Beaten three lengths off this exact mark at Thirsk 19 days ago, Thankfully showed consistency there but needs to find more to trouble this field — effective at today's trip on suitable going, yet our figures place it well down the rankings.

runners_data.name: Dream Camp
runners_data.comment: Broke through with a comfortable maiden win at Southwell over 1m last time, handled today's trip and going conditions before, and represents a strong training operation with potential for more now entering handicaps — but ranked 27 of 30 on our figures, making it hard to fancy at likely odds.

races.paceDynamic: Awaken is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 30-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine pace pressure from another pure lead horse — she can dictate every fraction at Ascot's straight mile on Good to Firm ground, controlling tempo without being harassed. Behind her, a cluster of prominently-raced types including Mubasimah, Hope Queen, Seet, Just Call Me Angel and Repel will jostle for the limited early positions behind the leader, while Brigid's Well, Blingy's Sister, Tavana, Harlequin Angel, Bintaziza and others are true front-runners or prominent types who are redistributed rearward on the map because 30 horses cannot all race prominently — those drawn widest or slowest away will effectively race against their nature. This field holds far more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate; of those redistributed, Brigid's Well (Jamie Spencer, capable of finding gaps), Glyfada and Green Carrera are best placed to reclaim something closer to their natural position. With one sustainable lead set by Awaken and a compressed midfield of reluctant hold-up types, this race shape heavily favours horses with natural tactical speed who can sit prominently in the first five to six, travel within themselves and pick up powerfully in Ascot's final two furlongs — the prominent-to-midfield profile with proven good-to-firm form is the sweet spot.

races.name: King Edward VII Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)

runners_data.name: Ancient Egypt
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's colt has strong staying form — three wins at 8-10f on Good, solid sim-going record — but is a natural prominent racer operating in a hold-up slot here because the field is overloaded with pace types; David Egan will need to find a way to travel comfortably in rear, and the style mismatch tempers confidence despite the course-appropriate profile.
runners_data.comment: Ran in the Derby at Epsom last time — Group 1 level, even if well beaten eighth — and three wins in the last five starts underline real ability, with the return to quick ground a major plus; consistency remains the question.

runners_data.name: Causeway
runners_data.note: The A P O'Brien/Ryan Moore combination with a horse carrying winning form at 1m on Good that steps up to 1m4f; confirmed sole front-runner who can dictate fractions entirely on his own terms, though his sim-going record is limited to two runs and he has had 27 days off — fitness is the one query.
runners_data.comment: Four wins in his last five starts — the latest a battling Group 3 success at the Curragh — signal a colt in red-hot form, and the step up to 12f looks a natural progression for this imposing type; the first-time hood is the one thing to watch.

runners_data.name: Echo Of Stars
runners_data.note: Oliver Cole's gelding won over 10f on Good last time, making him a live course-and-distance type, yet he is a prominent racer who cannot secure his natural berth and will be shuffled to midfield in the early stages; Jamie Spencer is an adept handler of tactical races but the race shape asks Echo Of Stars to do something he hasn't done before.
runners_data.comment: Broke its duck at Chepstow 21 days ago, wearing a tongue-tie again today, but stepping into novice company rather than a handicap where connections might have exploited that win more ruthlessly — our figures rank it last of six, making it hard to fancy despite genuine course-and-distance versatility.

runners_data.name: Golden Story
runners_data.note: K R Burke's colt has won at 11f on Good and shapes as a genuine mile-and-a-half horse stepping into Group 2 company; Clifford Lee rides, and while Golden Story is a keen prominent type who has been pushed back on the map by the congested pace, his finishing kick over this trip is a real asset if he can get a smooth passage.
runners_data.comment: Competitive recent form — two wins from three latest starts including a Listed success last time — but our figures rank Golden Story fifth of six here, making it tough to fancy at this level despite the horse being open to further progress.

runners_data.name: Venetian Prince
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's colt is the only runner here with a confirmed Ascot win on his CV (1m3f on Heavy), giving him a meaningful course edge; Jason Watson has partnered him before and he is a natural prominent type who fits the map cleanly — 17 days since last run is not a concern given Balding's form, and his second run at 11f on Tapeta showed progression.
runners_data.comment: Venetian Prince arrives on the back of a neck Group 2 success at San Siro 17 days ago, handled by a trainer with a strong record at this track, and the wide range of conditions he handles — heavy to fast — adds versatility; first-time headgear is the unknown, and Italian form may not fully translate here.

runners_data.name: Water To Wine
runners_data.note: The Gosden yard sends out an unbeaten colt — two wins at 11f, including on Good — but Water To Wine is a natural prominent racer who cannot hold that position in this crowded pace map and will find himself racing in midfield; William Buick's presence is a significant positive, and the raw form reads well, but limited experience (just two runs) in a Group 2 against established performers is a genuine risk.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins — including a dominant 11-length success last time — mark Water To Wine as the one to beat here, with trainer form strong and a genuine shot at a first Group victory now looking within reach over this trip.

races.paceDynamic: Causeway is the confirmed pace-setter here and, with Ryan Moore aboard for Aidan O'Brien, he is likely to dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo on Good to Firm ground over 1m4f at Ascot — a surface and distance that rewards relaxed, well-rated travellers rather than tearaway front-runners. The field is saturated with prominent types: Water To Wine, Golden Story, and Echo Of Stars are all natural prominent racers who cannot all secure their favoured berth, meaning at least two or three will be forced to race slightly further back than they would choose, and Ancient Egypt is similarly redistributed to a hold-up role. With Causeway uncontested and able to control fractions, the pace is unlikely to be truly severe, making it a tactical affair where the horse who travels best into the straight and quickens most fluently will dominate. This race shape strongly favours a prominent runner who can sit just off Causeway's shoulder, get a clear run into the straight, and produce a decisive mid-to-late burst — in other words, a high-class, well-ridden stalker rather than a deep closer or a pure leader who has already used energy up front.
