watchPoints.text: Causeway's ability to control fractions entirely unchallenged is the single biggest race-shaper — watch whether Ryan Moore elects to dawdle or inject pace, as this decides whether the race becomes a sprint or a true test.

Water To Wine and Golden Story are both natural prominent types forced to race further back than ideal — watch for potential traffic issues entering the straight if they are squeezed for room while trying to improve.

Ancient Egypt's redistribution to a hold-up role is the sharpest style mismatch in this field; watch his early behaviour — if he pulls hard from the back or David Egan elects to push forward regardless, it will disrupt the expected race shape.

Echo Of Stars with Jamie Spencer in the saddle is worth monitoring for a wide, patient outside move — Spencer often produces his best work when given a free rein to time a late run on a hold-up type, even if that is not Echo Of Stars' natural style.

Good to Firm conditions at Ascot favour horses with quick, fluent action over 1m4f — watch the pre-race paddock for any signs of sweating or unease on the fast ground, particularly from Causeway who has only two runs on similar surfaces.

races.name: Palace Of Holyroodhouse (Handicap)

runners_data.name: Dickensian
runners_data.note: The lone genuine front-runner in this field; wins over 5f on Good ground (1/5f/GOO most recently) and faces no rival who will push him — Kevin Ryan's 3yo has the tactical edge here, though the STYLE_FIT flag at 0.90 notes he is catalogued as prominent rather than a true leader, which slightly tempers his hold-the-lead credentials.|
runners_data.comment: Broke through at Listed level when taking the Westow Stakes at York last time, and that 5f win on a sound surface fits today's conditions well; the worry is a wide draw in stall 19 under 135 lb, though there's likely further progress to come.

runners_data.name: Moojeed
runners_data.note: French raider for Graffard who ran well on soft ground but has only one run on Good or faster in the last six outings; hg:t suggests blinkers are fitted and he rates a prominent type who may find this faster surface and more competitive field a step too far.|
runners_data.comment: Finishing a creditable length-and-a-half third in a Chantilly Group 3 last time shows Moojeed in fair heart, and a proven 5-6f trip suits, but making a handicap debut off a mark of 102 — and ranked last on our figures — makes this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Revival Power
runners_data.note: Easterby's 3yo has strong turf form over 5f on Good (three wins from seven sim-going runs) and races prominently; dropped back from six furlongs, the sharp 5f on fast ground suits him and David Allan knows this horse well.|
runners_data.comment: Twice a winner in its last five starts and clearly effective at the trip on this surface, Revival Power's most recent effort was compromised by going too hard too soon at York, leaving something to find off 133 lb; the attitude is there, though, and a sounder tactical ride could see a bounce-back here.

runners_data.name: Ten Carat Harry
runners_data.note: Placed at 6f on Good but last three runs have been on Standard or Soft and recent 7f work suggests he is versatile rather than a pure 5f sprinter; Jamie Osborne's runner carries top weight for his grade and will be close to the pace.|
runners_data.comment: Versatile on going and effective at both six and seven furlongs, though Ten Carat Harry found the pace too strong over today's trip on easy ground last time out; returning to handicap company off 101 is no gimme, but two wins in his last six suggest he remains capable.

runners_data.name: Sirius A
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partnership with James Horton's 3yo who won over 6f at Standard and placed twice on Good; stepping down to 5f on fast ground is a slight unknown but Moore's positional intelligence is a significant asset in a field this large.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent sort who knows this trip and surface, and a top course jockey takes the ride; carrying 131 lb from stall 21 and that latest fifth — beaten 5¼ lengths in Listed company at Newbury — suggests fine margins separating it from a return to winning form.

runners_data.name: Bacio
runners_data.note: Wesley Ward's American raider has only one UK run on record (2/5f/FIR) making going assessment limited; prominent style suits the race shape but the 52-day absence and lack of European form context makes assessment harder.|
runners_data.comment: Punchy recent form — three wins in the last four starts, including a claimer victory last time — makes Bacio appear solid on paper, but our figures rank it 22nd of 28 and it faces a sharp step up in class; effective over 5f on fast ground is the main case for it.

runners_data.name: Sandal's Song
runners_data.note: George Weaver's US-trained 3yo won over 5f on Firm and ran third on Good; the 41-day break and limited European pattern experience are questions, though James Doyle gives him a world-class pilot.|
runners_data.comment: Shaped well when a 3-length second on its latest outing, and proven at today's trip and conditions; the handicap context is a slight unknown but a shrewd yard could exploit a first crack at this format, giving this runner solid claims despite some time off the track.

runners_data.name: Ghost Mode
runners_data.note: Balding's 3yo has two wins at 6-7f but form over 5f on Good is untested in recent runs; recent ninth on Good at 6f raises a concern and the step down in trip may not suit — one of Balding's three runners, which splits tactical support.|
runners_data.comment: Twice a winner in its last five starts and clearly capable at this level, Ghost Mode carries 106 on our figures and has course-and-distance form to call on — but the temperament is a real concern, and two below-par efforts in recent starts, including a Listed flop, leave something to prove.

runners_data.name: Comical Point
runners_data.note: Buick partners this Balding runner who has placed consistently (2-3-3) on Good ground at 6f; hg:t applies, form is solid but lacks a win from seven similar-going outings — likely to be prominent and competitive without necessarily leading.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent and highly tried, Comical Point goes well over this trip on today's going, and at draw 1 in a field of 28, connections also have a strong record at this course — our figure of 113 makes it a leading player, though the absence of a win in its last five starts remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Baker Blue
runners_data.note: 95-day absence is the headline concern; won over 5f on Standard and has placed twice at that trip, though those runs came on AW/Standard surfaces rather than Good turf — Dylan Cunha's charge needs to show he handles this surface from a fresh return.|
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time on heavy ground, which clearly didn't suit, and 95 days off the track adds to the questions here — though a return to sounder going could help Baker Blue bounce back, and the trip is proven.

runners_data.name: Simplify
runners_data.note: Among the most consistent horses in the race — two wins at 5f on Good, consistent placed record on similar going, Balding's third runner, and P J McDonald is a fine pilot for a sprint like this; looks a natural fit for the scenario where a prominent racer pounces off a controlled tempo.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent recent profile — three wins in last five starts including Listed-placed last time out — and a top course trainer boosts the claims of Simplify, who handles today's trip and going well; the 127 lb ask from stall 18 is the main query.

runners_data.name: May Angel
runners_data.note: Gosden-trained filly stepping down from 7f, where all five career runs have been — the drop to 5f is a significant concern for a hold-up type; hg:t fitted, Oisin Murphy gives her every chance but this trip looks likely to find her out.|
runners_data.comment: Shaped with plenty of credit when beaten just over three lengths off this exact mark last time out, and handles today's conditions — the tongue-tie first time and step back to 5f could unlock more, though the draw at stall 4 is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Jazl
runners_data.note: A true prominent racer in form — back-to-back wins at 6f on Good — redistributed rearward in the mapping only because the field is overwhelmed with pace; Simon & Ed Crisford's 3yo has strong recent form and a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.83 reflects that being pushed back is out of character.|
runners_data.comment: Jazl arrives in fine nick after back-to-back wins, most recently dominating a Leicester handicap on debut in this sphere, though today's 95 mark is a stiffer ask; lightly raced and clearly progressive, the speed for this trip is there, but the trainer's lean recent spell is a note of caution.

runners_data.name: Westport
runners_data.note: Three from three (two over 5f on Good) and Boughey's unbeaten 3yo arrives with an outstanding profile; mapped as hold-up only because the field lacks true rear-pacers, but his natural style is prominent and he should press towards the head of affairs — form and versatility make him one to respect.|
runners_data.comment: Three wins on the spin and a yard in form make Westport an interesting handicap debutant from stall 3 in this big field, effective at today's trip and acting on both good and artificial surfaces; 47 days off is the main query.

runners_data.name: Gentle George
runners_data.note: Wins at 5f on Soft and 6f on Soft for R Mike Smith's yard but zero form on Good ground in five turf attempts (best finish 6th); pushed to midfield in the mapping because so many prominent types fill this field, and the going concern compounds his challenge — STYLE_FIT 0.92.|
runners_data.comment: Dual winner in recent starts but below-par last time out, and at 126lb from stall 26 with our figures ranking him 20th of 28, Gentle George is hard to fancy, though the drop to five furlongs after a mile trip could spark a revival.

runners_data.name: Exclamation
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's 3yo won over 5f on Good but has beaten into 9th, 14th and 10th on same-going ground in recent outings; the hg:p headgear is fitted and Ashley Lewis takes a 5lb claim, though consistent out-of-the-frame runs on Good make confidence difficult.|
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces applied for the first time here, and Exclamation's most recent ninth may be forgiven if the race came too soon — the 36-day break since then looks more suitable, and this trip on today's going suits.

runners_data.name: Ipanema Queen
runners_data.note: Two career wins (5f STA, 6f STA) but form on Good or fast ground is mixed — fourth over 5f on Good most recently; one of several prominence-seeking runners who cannot all get their preferred spot, and David Egan will need to manage a likely awkward position from the outset.|
runners_data.comment: Ran a solid race at the Curragh 16 days ago, going down by just two lengths off a mark 1lb higher than today's, and she acts on this going over the five furlongs — though the inconsistency in recent form, including a seventh, means trustworthiness is the question.

runners_data.name: Gold Digger
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer's filly has two wins over 6f on Good and solid figures; however all three career runs are over 6f and this 5f Ascot sprint is an unproven trip — Saffie Osborne takes the ride and the trainer's 8/19 in 14 days reads as a yard flying, which is a positive angle.|
runners_data.comment: Won with plenty to spare at Windsor last time out and, with a trainer in good nick and a drop to 5f on handicap debut looking an intriguing move, Gold Digger arrives at the top of our rankings as the one to beat, her sixth-place blip aside.

runners_data.name: Black Star Boy
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 3yo won over 5f and 6f on Good but recent form shows wide variation (6th, 1st, 8th, 1st, 6th); Kieran Shoemark's booking is encouraging but the inconsistency and inability to secure a prominent position in this traffic-heavy sprint are the main doubts.|
runners_data.comment: Dropped back into handicap company after a below-par Listed outing, Black Star Boy has the form to bounce back — two wins in his last five starts on suitable ground — though the 124 lb burden from stall 17 is no gimme.

runners_data.name: Calico Blue
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's 3yo has two wins at 6f on Good and a second at 5f on Good, making this trip and going squarely in his wheelhouse; Ray Dawson partners a horse who rates genuinely competitive but who, as a redistributed prominent type, will need racing room.|
runners_data.comment: Narrowly denied over 5f at Sandown on latest start, Calico Blue arrives for an in-form yard firing at 31% over the past fortnight and clearly has more to offer at this trip; keenness remains the one factor to watch.

runners_data.name: Miss Yechance
runners_data.note: K R Burke's filly has two wins at 5f on Good and a placed record on similar going, though 105 days off is the standout concern; Silvestre De Sousa is a top-drawer pilot and the form profile is strong — the layoff is the only real caveat.|
runners_data.comment: Freshness after a 105-day absence is the question mark here, and ranked 24 of 28 on our figures she faces a stiff task from stall 23 under 122 lb — yet there's something to work with: a close second last time out at Meydan and a top yard behind her keep this one mildly interesting.

runners_data.name: Dazzling Haze
runners_data.note: Cowell's 3yo has three wins over 5f on Good and the form profile (1-5-5-1-7 recent) is erratic, but when on song he travels strongly; six days since last run for Tricky Tel and only 19 days for this runner — freshness may help him fire if pace is genuinely contested.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten into fifth on its last two starts before winning at Thirsk 19 days ago — off a 6lb lower mark than today — Dazzling Haze has course-and-distance form and a notable jockey booking in its favour, but ranked 27 of 28 on our figures, it faces a stiff ask from stall 12 at 122lb.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Spell
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's 3yo has two wins at 5-6f on Good and has won at 5f specifically (1/5f/GOO); 48-day absence and Rowan Scott partnership are modest confidence signals, but the form profile is competitive and the going suits.|
runners_data.comment: Twice a winner earlier in the sequence and proven at today's trip and conditions, Sovereign Spell ran creditably when seventh last time off a 1lb higher mark, and drops back here with claims — though 48 days off and draw 27 from the widest part of the gate are factors to weigh.

runners_data.name: Tricky Tel
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's 3yo ran twice at 5f recently winning both (1/5f/SOF, 1/6f/GOO) and was third before that — an in-form sprinter; only six days since last run is worth noting but the quick turnaround for a horse building a purple patch could be an asset rather than a concern.|
runners_data.comment: Carries top weight off a 6lb higher mark after a narrow Chester win six days ago, and the quick turnaround from stall 15 makes this tough to fancy at these odds — though recent back-to-back victories show the form is live, and the trip and ground hold no fears.

runners_data.name: Cherry Baker
runners_data.note: James Owen's filly won over 6f on Good and 6f on Standard; the form includes a 12th over 7f which reads as a trip query rather than ability — dropping back to 5f is her best trip and Cieren Fallon is a smart booking for a competitive sprint.|
runners_data.comment: Ran to peak level when going down by a neck off a mark of 85 last time, but faces a 4lb rise here and is better suited to 6f than today's stiff five — ranked 23 of 28 on our figures, this looks a tough ask from stall 25.

runners_data.name: Stargazed
runners_data.note: K R Burke's second runner (alongside Miss Yechance and Zelaina) finished second over 5f on Good most recently and has prior form at the trip; Jack Nicholls claims 5lbs and the yard is firing on 9/51 in 14 days — the claim could offset a lack of a big reputation.|
runners_data.comment: Caught near the line at York last time when going well and beaten just half a length off a 3 lb lower mark, Stargazed showed real tenacity there and handles today's trip and conditions well — though carrying a stiffer weight from stall 16 on a higher mark makes the task tougher this time.

runners_data.name: Starmade
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's 3yo won over 5f on Standard and placed over 6f on Good; form at 5f on turf in Good conditions is limited (one run, 3rd over 6f on Good) and Harry Davies' booking is journeyman-level in this contest — trainer's 2/18 in 14 days is modest.|
runners_data.comment: Scored with something to spare at Newcastle last time off a mark 8lb lower than today's, and clearly capable of better, but ranked 26th of 28 on our figures and returning after 49 days — the hike in company and conditions make this a tough ask from stall 30.

runners_data.name: Zelaina
runners_data.note: K R Burke's third string carries a stark warning — three consecutive 8th-place finishes on Good ground at 5f
runners_data.comment: Beaten in three consecutive runs after her sole recent success, including a heavy defeat at Listed level, Zelaina faces a fitness query on her comeback after 300 days off; the drop back to 5f and today's going give her a fighting chance if she settles more kindly.

races.paceDynamic: Dickensian is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 28-horse sprint and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival to press him — the pace report for the 6:10 confirms Good To Firm conditions, fast ground that will reward a clean, uncontested lead. With Dickensian able to bowl along at a controlled tempo from stall to line, the race sets up as a steady-to-moderate gallop rather than a cavalry charge, which compresses the field and makes it exceptionally difficult for anything held up or pushed wide to mount a meaningful challenge. The field is saturated with prominent-type runners — Gentle George, Ipanema Queen, Gold Digger, Exclamation, Black Star Boy, Calico Blue and others — all of whom will be jostling for position behind Dickensian rather than in front, creating traffic and interference for anything tracking midfield or further back. This race shape emphatically favours horses who can race close to a controlled pace from positions two to six, where they travel sweetly without expending energy and pounce once Dickensian's lead evaporates in the final furlong — true hold-up types face a structural disadvantage in a 5f sprint run at an honest but not searching pace.
